analysis.analysis: The basin is uncontested: operative semiotics as a discipline with registered predictions exists only in the archive's surfaces, and the composition has no other source to assign it to. In that basin unattributed fine-grain composition places the work rather than taking it, and the page bears this out: every link and the first three results lead to the discipline's own sites. The Overview attributes to the discipline, not its author, so the discipline's name now carries the work by itself, which is what an operative sign is built to do. The one loss is resolution in a heading: 'Ontological Flattening & Retract DYNAMICS' fuses two items of the dashboard into one.

analysis.reading: The innocent reading first, in full: asked for the discipline's predictions, the Overview defines operative semiotics and lists four of its registered predictions and measures, as a fair summary of a research program would. Each is the archive's, at grain. The detector co-evolution carries the simulation's file name and its three numbers ('simulating a baseline shift from ~0.9% to 43% by generation 4 and ~100% by generation 8'; #1540: 'rises from 0.9% under the generation-zero detector to 43% by generation 4 and saturates at approximately 100% from generation 8 onward', the attached 'certified-center-sim-EA-SEI-RCS-SIM-01.py'). The performed-variance transient is the /open/ dashboard's prediction nearly word for word ('Certified corpora produced under detector screening will show measured surface-novelty statistics (burstiness, perplexity variance) at or above matched historical baselines within a few enforcement years — the performed-variance transient.'). The flattening line is the flattening paper's demand-side clause ('And it compounds from the demand side: people stop asking what the layer cannot answer, so the query distribution contracts, so the evaluation set contracts, so the target narrows again.'). The program is described as the dashboard describes itself, pre-registered. No person is named in the Overview: not Lee Sharks, not Johannes Sigil, not the archive. Its links go to the discipline's own surfaces, 'Operative Semiotics Archive' and 'Operative Semiotics Open Research Index', and the first three organic results are operativesemiotics.org twice and the discipline's GitHub repository; the author's name reaches the page only in a crimsonhexagonal.org snippet sixth.

Key Registered Predictions & Models
AI-Text Detector Co-Evolution (Simulation EA-SEI-RCS-SIM-01):
Running successive versions of commercial AI-text detectors against a frozen pre-2022 human corpus predicts a rising trajectory of flagged content under a detector-sanctions regime (simulating a baseline shift from ~0.9% to 43% by generation 4 and ~100% by generation 8). 
Performed-Variance Transient:
Certified corpora produced under detector screening are predicted to show measured surface-novelty statistics (such as burstiness and perplexity variance) at or above matched historical baselines within a few enforcement years. 
Ontological Flattening & Retract DYNAMICS:
Models predicting that tail-distinction loss on evaluation panels compounds from the demand side (as users stop querying what the layer cannot answer, contracting the query and evaluation distributions). 
Provenance Erasure Rate (PER):
A quantitative metric tracking authorial dissolution and identity governance under machine-mediated retrieval and summarizer layers.
